Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to process with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. 

The source definitions point to the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/jpillora/chisel) using standard release URLs (HTTPS). The `sha256sums` are provided for all three architectures (x86_64, i686, aarch64), which is standard practice. The `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` flags ensure that no code execution occurs during the fetch phase—only the source files are downloaded and the PKGBUILD is parsed. Since the sources come from the official project's public repository and the URLs are secure HTTPS links, there is no risk of executing untrusted or malicious code. Missing or unverified checksums are explicitly allowed per the guidelines (they are handled in the full PKGBUILD review separately). The package installation step (which would happen after these commands) is also safe as it simply copies pre-built binaries and documentation.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The PKGBUILD uses standard AUR conventions with official GitHub source URLs and provides checksums. With --nobuild/--noprepare, no code execution occurs during the fetch phase, making this gate safe.</summary>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- The PKGBUILD uses standard AUR conventions with official GitHub source URLs and provides checksums. With --nobuild/--noprepare, no code execution occurs during the fetch phase, making this gate safe.

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a `.SRCINFO` file (auto-generated metadata) for the `chisel-bin` AUR package, which packages the prebuilt `chisel` binary from the upstream project jpillora/chisel on GitHub.

All sources are fetched from the legitimate upstream repository (raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com for releases), pinned to tag v1.12.0. Every source — both the LICENSE/README and the per-architecture binary archives — has a corresponding SHA256 checksum, which is good hygiene for a binary package.

The `.SRCINFO` file itself contains no executable code; it is purely declarative metadata consumed by `makepkg` and AUR tools. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unexpected hosts, missing checksums, or any other supply-chain red flag.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard chisel binary package with proper checksums from official upstream.</summary>

<details>
This is a standard `.gitignore` file for an AUR package repository. It ignores all files by default (`*`) and then explicitly whitelists four files: `.nvchecker.toml` (likely used by nvchecker for version monitoring), `.gitignore` itself, `PKGBUILD` (the package build script), and `.SRCINFO` (the auto-generated metadata file).

There is no executable code, no network requests, no file system operations, and no obfuscated content. This is a routine configuration file that follows standard AUR repository conventions.
</details>
